description: Alert schedules (RFC 0003 §4.3): candidate alerts from known events, the half-open range, the query bounded by maximumReminderOffset, owning days across midnight, Jumu'ah and per-day settings, and the canonical order.

vectors.description: Every prayer with an at-time alert, a 10-minute before-reminder and a 5-minute after-reminder over one day: fifteen alerts by fire date. Sunrise has no settings.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.3 Candidates; proposal §7.5 (fifteen requests for a full day).

vectors.description: The range starts at Dhuhr and ends at Asr: Dhuhr's at-time alert at the start is in, Asr's at-time alert at the end is out, and the reminders between are in.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.3: the fire-date range [start, end) is half-open.

vectors.description: Two short ranges: one holds only Dhuhr's before-reminder, though Dhuhr is after the range; the other only Isha's after-reminder, though Isha is before it.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.3 Candidates; proposal §7.5: query events before and after the range to include after-reminders of earlier prayers and before-reminders of later ones.

vectors.description: The range holds only Isha's after-reminder at 20:35; Isha at 20:30 is before it.
Fajr's before-reminder and Isha's after-reminder are exactly maximumReminderOffset (two hours) away from their prayers, and both are found: 02:11 and 22:30.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.3: the query reads start − m through end + m, so an offset equal to m is inside it.

vectors.description: The range ends at 02:11, the fire date of Fajr's two-hour before-reminder: Fajr is read (04:11 is the query's end), but its reminder is at the excluded end.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.3: events(from: start − m, through: end + m) includes its end; the fire-date range excludes its own.

vectors.description: In Edinburgh at midsummer, 21 June's Isha is at 00:15 on the 22nd. Its before-reminder at 23:45, its alert and its after-reminder at 00:30 all belong to 21 June. The 22nd's Fajr reminder at 01:35 belongs to the 22nd.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.2: the identity's day is the event's owning day, even after midnight (RFC 0001 §4.3).

vectors.description: In Kazan under the middle-of-the-night rule, 20 June's Fajr is at 23:45 on the 19th, the instant of the 19th's Isha. Fajr's alerts belong to 20 June though they fire on the 19th, and at 23:45 the 19th's Isha alert comes first.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.2 (owning days; order by day, then prayer, then kind); Vectors/calculation/owning-days.json for the instants.

vectors.description: Friday 5 June declares Jumu'ah: its Dhuhr uses the Jumu'ah settings (45-minute reminder, a named sound, a silent reminder). Thursday's Dhuhr uses Dhuhr's.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.1: settings are asked per subject, whose observance comes from the event.

vectors.description: The same settings on a Friday whose timetable declares nothing: Dhuhr's settings apply.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.1; RFC 0001 §4.3 rule 11: a Friday is a date, Jumu'ah is declared.

vectors.description: One day has its own settings (a reminder before Fajr, after Isha); the days around it use the usual ones.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.1: the subject carries its owning day.

vectors.description: Maghrib's 45-minute after-reminder and Isha's 45-minute before-reminder both fire at 19:45: Maghrib's comes first, by prayer order.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.2 Order: fire date, then identity (day, prayer, kind).

vectors.description: Sunrise can have alerts too (here a silent alert and a reminder 20 minutes before), and each alert carries the sound of its kind.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.1: subjects are any PrayerKind; each kind has its own sound.

vectors.description: An end before the start counts as the start: no alerts, and an empty requested range.
Settings that are nil for every prayer: no alerts and no gaps, though the timetable has a missing day in range.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.3: a gap of a prayer whose settings are nil makes no alert gap.
